newsitem.title: UK: Consortium issues junk bond to fund BBC purchase.
newsitem.headline: Consortium issues junk bond to fund BBC purchase.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston has arranged a high-yielding sterling bond as part of financing for the purchase of the BBC's domestic radio and television transmission network, the bank said on Wednesday.
A 125 million stg 10-year bond was launched in the name of Castle Transmission Services, an international consortium, at a spread of 195 basis points over gilts.
The proceeds will help fund CTS' acquisition of the BBC's transmission network. Roadshows for the offering were held last week.
High-yielding debt, or junk bonds in market parlance, is issued by unrated or low-rated companies.
They provide investors with a substantial yield pick-up over more conventional bonds launched by more highly-rated banks and companies.
European investors are turning to high-risk debt in an effort to boost returns on their portfolios in a low-inflation, low-interest rate environment.
The first European junk bonds were issued in April when two companies launched mark-denominated deals, the first non-dollar transactions. Both fundings were heavily oversubscribed.
The junk bond market is well-established in the U.S., with around $210 billion outstanding.

Castle Transmission Services is a consortium led by Castle Tower Corporation (CTC) of the U.S. which bought the state-owned BBC's domestic radio and television transmission network for 244 million stg in February.

The consortium, which also includes TeleDiffusion de France, a subsidiary of the France Telecom Group, Candover Investments Plc and Berkshire Partners LLC, has a 10-year contract for transmission of BBC analogue television and radio services.
The British government outlined proposals for the sale of the transmission businesses in November 1995.
